quote:
Suppression of herbaceous vegetation through
cutting positively affected species richness of broadleaved
seedlings in pasture (ID8; Table 1).
raw_name: species richness of broadleaved seedlings in pasture
attribution: Holl, K. D., M. E. Loik, E. H. V. Lin, and I. A. Samuels (2000). Tropical montane forest restoration in Costa Rica: overcoming barriers to dispersal and establishment. Restoration Ecology 8:339–349. Review Table 1 study ID 8; original not acquired/registered in current SRC/queue.

relationship.outcome_raw: Broadleaved seedling species richness after cutting herbaceous vegetation in abandoned pasture compared with unmanipulated control; no effect magnitude transcribed.

context.region: Southern Costa Rica tropical montane pasture
context.practice_as_described: Assisted natural regeneration by cutting competing herbaceous vegetation in abandoned pasture; comparator is unmanipulated pasture (review effect-size inclusion rule, PDF2). Cutting suppresses herbaceous competition rather than planting trees.
context.note: PDF4 printed673 Richness; review Table1 ID8 maps to Holl et al.2000, Costa Rica. PDF5 identifies six-month response and broadleaved cover/richness. This is broadleaved seedling richness, not proven native forest-tree richness, long-term composition, or canopy cover. Source review re-signs effect sizes to restoration progress; this claim uses explicit positive richness wording instead of generic g* sign. Same primary study underlies other review outcomes and Shono cited mechanisms; count once by lineage. Primary article not directly inspected; no significance or numeric effect inferred.
